ws1.fourth_defect: GLOBAL (O4): global vitti holder assigned a kosh in set_holder(), read holder[100] in mukhya() -> prints 0, exit 0 (silent over-read). Most distinct because it is inter-function (not in the brief's WS1 list, which is all intra-function). The per-function table cannot track globals at all.

not_defects.assign_mala_to_kosh: a = m (mala); a = k (kosh, via assignment); a[100] refuses (bounds check, exit 1) - assignment TO kosh DOES mark, so this direction is correct
not_defects.kosh_parameter: prakriya foo(kosh k) { k[100] } refuses (mala ank seema atikram, exit 1) - parameter type is in its declaration, not in kosh_vars, so it bounds-checks directly, correct
not_defects.redeclare_both_directions: vitti a = k; vitti a = m (and reverse) both compile-refuse E_DUPLICATE_NAME (punah ghoshana 'a'; hint: use a = ... to give a new value) - redeclaration forbidden, so never-cleared table cannot be stale via redeclaration
not_defects.scope_both_directions: Outer raw + inner kosh via yadi block (and reverse) both compile-refuse E_DUPLICATE_NAME (inner declaration refused) - Sutram has no block scoping for names (one namespace per function, duplicates refused), so the table CANNOT confuse scopes (scopes do not exist for names)
not_defects.ternary_in_bounds_both_branches: a = c ? k : p; c=1 -> a[0]=11 (correct); c=0 -> a[0]=77 (correct), exit 0 - ternary assignments are NOT marked (not a bare variable), so they use raw code, which works for in-bounds reads on both kosh and raw buffers (by accident for kosh); out-of-bounds is a defect (O5 below)
not_defects.vitti_parameter: prakriya foo(vitti x) compile-refuses (vyakaran dosh, vitti not a valid parameter type) - vitti parameters do not exist, so the vitti-parameter door does not exist; use a kosh parameter (above, which bounds-checks)

ws1.verdict: Table is per-function, name-keyed, set only from a bare variable, never cleared, blind to control flow - and every one of those properties is a defect: (1) set only from bare variables -> call results, mala cells, kosh cells, ternary expressions, and globals are never marked (5 silent over-read doors, all print 0, exit 0); (2) never cleared -> kosh->non-kosh reassignment keeps stale kosh marking and crashes (kosh->raw straight-line (S1, old), kosh->mala assignment (S2, new), loop reassignment (S3, new trigger)); (3) per-function -> globals never marked in any function's table (same-function or inter-function); (4) name-keyed + no block scoping -> redeclaration and scope confusion are NOT defects (both refused E_DUPLICATE_NAME, clean); (5) parameter type in declaration -> kosh parameters bounds-check correctly (not a defect); vitti parameters do not exist (not a defect). 8 defect instances total (3 segfaults + 5 over-reads); at least 5 new beyond Claude's three.

ws2.prints: Exactly '0' (no trailing newline) and exits 0. The kosh holds 11 at [0] and has length 4 (capacity 4); index 100 is past its length, but because a was assigned from a call result (not a bare variable), kosh_vars never marked it, so no bounds check fires, and the raw load reads 0 from zero-filled region memory beyond the elements - a wrong number that looks right, with no error and no crash. (Mala-cell and kosh-cell versions are equally small at 10 lines with a newline likha; the call-result version without it is 9 lines, so it is the smallest.)
ws2.program: prakriya make_kosh() { kosh k[4]; kosh_kship(k, 11); nivartanam k } ; mukhya() { vitti a = make_kosh(); likha(a[100]) } - 9 lines, no trailing-newline likha

ws3.brief_premise_correction: Brief says 'That number has been quoted from a report and never independently measured.' WRONG (stale): Round 124 independently measured it on v298 (commit 69a03fc7, probe maxcap_alias2.sm: original 99, alias 41 stale, exit 0). This round re-verifies it on v300 (current main), so it has now been measured TWICE, on two versions, with the same result.
ws3.naming_note: In this probe a is the ALIAS (vitti a = k) and k is the ORIGINAL kosh, the reverse of R124's naming (where a = original, k = alias), so R124 reported a[0]=99 and k[0]=41 - same values, opposite names, same break. Naming chosen here to match the brief's question ('report what a[0] gives').
ws3.program: kosh k[4]; push 41 (1 element); vitti a = k (alias); push 4,194,305 more via k (total 4,194,306 elements, past the 4,194,304 -> 4,194,305 relocation point, where capacity doubling 4,194,304 -> 8,388,608 exceeds MAXCAP 8,388,603 and relocates); then post-relocation write k[0] = 99 (via the original); then read both
ws3.result: On v300 (0.1 s, exit 0): a[0] = 41 (stale, broken), k[0] = 99 (correct). The alias breaks at about 4,194,304 elements: after relocation, the original is updated but the alias keeps the old pointer, so the alias reads the old value (41) while the true value is 99. Brief asks 'report what a[0] gives': a[0] gives 41 (the stale value, not the current 99) - proving the alias broke.
